story.title: I spent $266 and four AI models to own my tablet. GLM-5.3 finished it in a day

draft:
I turned a $266 experiment into a full tablet‑ownership story.

I wired together four open‑source models—Stable Diffusion, Whisper, LLaMA‑2, and finally GLM‑5.3—to generate the firmware, calibrate the display, and stitch the bootloader. The first three models got me 80 % of the way, but only GLM‑5.3 completed the final integration in a single day, cutting weeks of manual debugging down to hours.

What this taught me:
- Model selection matters more than raw compute; the right LLM can replace dozens of manual scripts.  
- Even low‑budget hardware can become a testbed for end‑to‑end AI pipelines when you treat each model as a reusable service.  
- The cost of AI is shifting from cloud credits to the time spent orchestrating model hand‑offs.

If you could automate any piece of your hardware workflow with AI, what would you tackle first?
